comment:
* This class defines the interval for which the certificate is valid.
 *
 * @author Amit Kapoor
 * @author Hemma Prafullchandra
 * @see CertAttrSet

variables.name: IDENT
variables.comment:
* Identifier for this attribute, to be used with the
     * get, set, delete methods of Certificate, x509 type.

variables.name: NAME
variables.comment: * Sub attributes name for this CertAttrSet.

methods.name: private Date getNotBefore()
methods.comment: Returns the first time the certificate is valid.

methods.name: private Date getNotAfter()
methods.comment: Returns the last time the certificate is valid.

methods.name: private void construct(DerValue derVal) throws IOException
methods.comment: Construct the class from the DerValue

methods.name: public String toString()
methods.comment: * Return the validity period as user readable string.

methods.name: public void encode(OutputStream out) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Encode the CertificateValidity period in DER form to the stream.
     *
     * @param out the OutputStream to marshal the contents to.
     * @exception IOException on errors.

methods.name: public void set(String name, Object obj) throws IOException
public Date get(String name) throws IOException
public void delete(String name) throws IOException
public Enumeration<String> getElements()
methods.comment:
* Return an enumeration of names of attributes existing within this
     * attribute.

methods.name: public String getName()
methods.comment: * Return the name of this attribute.

methods.name: public void valid() throws CertificateNotYetValidException, CertificateExpiredException
methods.comment:
* Verify that the current time is within the validity period.
     *
     * @exception CertificateExpiredException if the certificate has expired.
     * @exception CertificateNotYetValidException if the certificate is not
     * yet valid.

methods.name: public void valid(Date now) throws CertificateNotYetValidException, CertificateExpiredException
methods.comment: * Verify that the passed time is within the validity period. * @param now the Date against which to compare the validity * period. * * @exception CertificateExpiredException if the certificate has expired * with respect to the Date supplied. * @exception CertificateNotYetValidException if the certificate is not * yet valid with respect to the Date supplied. *
